name: Gamechanger Audio Motor Synth (MKI)
description: Gamechanger Audio Motor Synth, the first model: every sound and global parameter of its manual's NRPN map, with Pull from its sound and global parameter dumps.

sources.title: Motor Synth MKI User Manual
sources.notes: The NRPN map (PDF pages 143 - 152) and the MIDI SysEx pages (PDF pages 152 - 155), read by tools/profiles/gamechanger/read-motor-maps.mjs from MOTOR-SYNTH-MKI-MANUAL.pdf (sha256 1d04ccf42c3cb691ed1cfd57af8177c540ff632dfc1af739bc7906fbf624bc32), https://gamechangeraudio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/MOTOR-SYNTH-MKI-MANUAL.pdf, linked from https://gamechangeraudio.com/support/msmki/. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/gamechanger/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/gamechanger/synths/, not this file.

Every parameter is a row of the NRPN map, sent as that NRPN on the base channel (the channel variable) with a 14-bit value: CC 99, CC 98, then CC 6 and CC 38, as the CC map gives data entry for NRPN. Its range is the row's MIDI DATA RANGE; where its PARAMETER VALUE RANGE differs, the value is shown in it (a FLOAT's, or an INTEGER's offset by the same width). The MIDI input filter must let NRPN through. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

Pull asks for the sound parameters (F0 7E 7F 07 02 00 21 6D F7, the "general channel" byte 7F, which the document says any channel answers) and for the global ones (…07 01…), and reads each dump, whose values are "in 14b format (MSB, LSB) ordered by NRPN ID [size: parameter count x 2 bytes]": the map's k-th row in NRPN order at bytes 2k and 2k + 1. That reading is the document's words taken as printed; a dump of any other length than the map's rows make is refused, so a firmware with other parameters is not misread. The sound parameter dump is 291 rows (582 bytes). The global parameter dump is 77 rows (154 bytes).

Left out, rows whose MIDI data range is not a range of 14-bit values (each still counted in its dump's order): 25 DETUNE MIN (MIDI data range 0 ... -1, value range -12 ... -1); 283 PWH R LOW (MIDI data range 0 ... 0, value range -12 ... 0); 8270 INIT PRESET REF (MIDI data range 0 ... 0x00FFFFFF, value range 0 ... 0x00FFFFFF).

Laid out with their MIDI data range, which the parameter value range does not match in width (so neither is shown as the other): 26 DETUNE MAX (1 ... 12 over 0 ... 12); 217 STEP MOD1 STEPS (2 ... 8 over 0 ... 8); 218 STEP MOD2 STEPS (2 ... 8 over 0 ... 8); 219 STEP MOD3 STEPS (2 ... 8 over 0 ... 8).

The device family and member codes the general info response prints are the same for the MKI and the MKII, so the identity does not tell them apart. (The MKII's basic MIDI implementation says Device Inquiry "No"; its SysEx document prints the request and the reply.)
The CC map gives many of these parameters a 14-bit controller pair as well (CC n, its LSB on n + 32); this profile sends the NRPNs, which cover every one.
